result.summary: The environment is dominated by a wide, multi-lane roadway with no visible marked crosswalks or pedestrian signals at the immediate intersection. While sidewalks are present, the lack of crossing infrastructure and potential sightline obstructions from mature trees create a high-exposure environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: Lack of marked crosswalks at a signalized intersection with multiple travel lanes increases pedestrian exposure and risk.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Dense foliage on the right corner may obscure pedestrians waiting to cross from the view of approaching motorists.

hazards.name: Wide Curb Radius
hazards.description: The intersection geometry appears to allow for high-speed right turns, increasing risk to pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks on all legs of the intersection to define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers and push buttons to provide clear crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to reduce crossing distance, improve sightlines, and slow turning vehicles.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, unmarked intersection with no visible traffic control or crossing aids. While a sidewalk exists on the residential side, the lack of protected crossing infrastructure and the scale of the roadway create a hostile environment for people walking.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: Large intersection with no painted crosswalks, forcing pedestrians to cross without a designated path or driver awareness.

hazards.name: Lack of Traffic Control
hazards.description: No stop signs or signals are visible to regulate vehicle flow or provide right-of-way to pedestrians at the intersection.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles and utility poles near the corner may block sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks on all legs of the intersection to define pedestrian space.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to reduce crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles at the intersection.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and properly sloped ramps at all crossing points to ensure accessibility.

result.summary: The environment is dominated by a multi-lane roadway with high-speed traffic and minimal pedestrian infrastructure. While a sidewalk and bike lane are present, there are no marked crossings or refuge islands, creating a hostile environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossing
hazards.description: No designated area for pedestrians to cross the multi-lane road.

hazards.name: Long crossing distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross four lanes of traffic without a refuge island.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked cars in the adjacent lot may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install high-visibility continental crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian paths.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a median refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Add curb extensions to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility.
